history.summary: IDENTITY UNCERTAIN - THIN SOURCING. The Ghatshila (Ghat Shila) Temple is a small rock temple on the ghat (hills) at Tuljapur, Dharashiv district. The dominant legend: Tulja Bhavani stood on these rocks (shila) to direct Lord Rama and Lakshmana toward Lanka as they searched for Sita; the rocks were sanctified by Rama's presence and offerings are made to Lord Rama there. However, one source instead describes a Mahishasurmardini Bhavani idol found in a local field as the shrine's deity - a CONFLICT that cannot be resolved from available sources (verify on site). The temple is described as a medieval-period rock shrine in a natural setting, visited mainly as a side shrine to the Tulja Bhavani pilgrimage; a children's park has reportedly been developed nearby by the temple trust. Founding date, builder, management and visiting hours are all UNVERIFIED.

name: Ghatshila Temple
town_description: Tuljapur is a temple town in Dharashiv district (formerly Osmanabad) of Maharashtra, set on the Yamunachala ranges at about 2,150 ft elevation, roughly 45 km from Solapur. It takes its name from the Tulja Bhavani temple and draws lakhs of pilgrims yearly from Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, who also regard the goddess as kuldevi. The town's other shrines - Ghat Shila, Chintamani, Dhakte Bhavani - plus the nearby Naldurg fort and Dharashiv caves make it a combined pilgrimage and heritage stop; it comes alive with fairs during Navratri.
